name: Smoky Sheet-Pan Chicken Fajitas
desc: Smoked-paprika chicken thighs roasted with three bell peppers and onion, served over cilantro-lime rice.

source.evidence: Searched smoky sheet-pan chicken thigh fajitas with smoked paprika over cilantro-lime rice; the sheet-pan fajita recipes found (Isabel Eats, Half Baked Harvest, Damn Delicious, Cooking in the Midwest) use tortillas and different spice ratios, and none pairs this rub with the rice.

ingredients.raw: 1 red bell pepper, sliced into strips
1 yellow bell pepper, sliced into strips
1 green bell pepper, sliced into strips
1 large yellow onion, sliced into strips

steps: Rice: combine the rice, water, and a pinch of salt in a pot. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce to low, and simmer until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender, about 18 min. Take off the heat and leave covered 5 min.

While the rice cooks, heat the oven to 425°F. Pound the chicken thighs to an even thickness and pat dry. Mix the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, oregano, and 1 tsp salt in a small bowl.
Toss the three peppers and the onion with the olive oil on a rimmed sheet pan, spreading them to the edges. Coat the chicken all over with the spice mix and set it in the center of the pan.
Roast until the chicken reads at least 165°F in the thickest part and the vegetables are charred at the edges, 16-18 min.
Rest the chicken 5 min, then slice into strips.
Fluff the rice and stir in the juice of 1 lime and the cilantro. Cut the other lime into wedges.
Pile the chicken and vegetables over the rice and finish with a squeeze of lime.
tips: The earlier version pulled the thighs at 160°F; thighs are safe at 165°F and turn more tender if they reach 175°F, so give them the extra minute or two if the vegetables allow.
